2026-08-27T16:00:48.5265802Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5266571Z 
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5267224Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5268360Z 
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5269099Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5270082Z 
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5273019Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5276506Z >
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5281299Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5286155Z >
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5287933Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5289498Z 
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5289882Z ### How to Use
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5290368Z 
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5294956Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5296447Z 
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5296818Z ```bash
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5298276Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5299762Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5301484Z ```
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5301929Z 
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5302493Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5303592Z ```bash
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5304688Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5306276Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5308194Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5309713Z ```
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5310140Z 
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5311308Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5313041Z ```bash
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5319305Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5320965Z ```
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5321413Z 
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5322072Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5324083Z ```bash
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5325179Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5326913Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5329033Z ```
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5329480Z 
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5330013Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5330862Z 
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5334114Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5337994Z 
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5338380Z ```bash
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5339313Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5341136Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5343292Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5343953Z 
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5344870Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5347269Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5349179Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5350165Z ```
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5350592Z 
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5352464Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5359162Z 
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5359573Z ```bash
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5360991Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5363408Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5365864Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5366777Z 
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5367808Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5369478Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5371750Z ```
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5372218Z 
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5372670Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5375734Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5378214Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5382541Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5385244Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5388218Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5389321Z 
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5389687Z ### Notes
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5390137Z 
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5391921Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5395308Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5398065Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5401170Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5405062Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5408607Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5411172Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-08-27T16:00:48.5413132Z </mcp-clis>
